items.summary: Visit https://www.younggoose.com/ and use code ASPREY10 to save on the skin longevity products discussed in this episode. Skin Longevity, Cellular Repair, Red Light Therapy & the Biology of Younger Skin with Young Goose Host Dave Asprey sits down with Amitay Eshel and Anastasia Khodzhaeva, co-founders of Young Goose, to explore the emerging science of skin longevity, cellular aging, mitochondrial function, exosomes, NAD+, red light therapy, and what it may take to keep skin functioning younger for longer. Anastasia is a biologist, biohacker, and co-CEO of Young Goose who began her career in biomedical research focused on liver fibrosis and breast cancer before moving into wellness, product development, and longevity-focused skincare. Amitay is co-founder and CEO of Young Goose and host of the Biohacking Beauty podcast, with more than a decade of experience across health, wellness, beauty, and business development. Together, they focus on applying longevity science and performance optimization to skin health. Amitay and Anastasia explain why wrinkles may be only one visible sign of a much deeper biological process involving declining cellular energy, weakened barrier function, oxidative stress, senescence, and changes in how skin cells repair themselves. They break down how newer approaches to skincare are moving beyond surface-level hydration toward targeting the cellular mechanisms associated with aging. items.title: Stubborn Belly Fat Starts In Your Liver (Here's The Fix)
items.summary: Visit LoveYourLiver.com and use code Dave2026 to access the special offer from de-liver-ance mentioned in this episode. Fatty Liver, GLP-1s, Alcohol, Hormones, Brain Fog, Weight Gain & Longevity Host Dave Asprey sits down with Siggi Clavien, Founder and CEO of The Liver Clinic and de-liver-ance, to explore why the liver may be one of the most overlooked organs in metabolism, hormone health, detoxification, brain function, weight management, and longevity. Siggi explains why fatty liver can develop without obvious symptoms and why someone can appear lean and healthy while still have significant liver fat. Drawing on thousands of liver scans, he shares what his team has observed in people whose blood markers appeared normal despite signs of fatty liver on imaging, and explains how tools such as FibroScan can reveal liver fat, stiffness, and fibrosis. Dave and Siggi go deep into triglycerides, cholesterol, insulin resistance, brain fog, weight gain, bile production, thyroid hormone activation, testosterone, estrogen metabolism, and liver regeneration. They also explore how alcohol, environmental chemicals, plastics, processed foods, artificial sweeteners, medications, and other exposures may place additional stress on the liver. items.title: TB-500 is finally entering human research. 🧬
items.summary: TB-500 has been discussed for years in the peptide and biohacking communities for its potential role in recovery, tissue repair and healing. But there's an important catch: much of the excitement surrounding TB-500 has been based on preclinical research, animal studies, and research involving its parent molecule, thymosin beta-4—not robust human clinical evidence for TB-500 itself. Now that's beginning to change. A human clinical trial involving TB-500 is giving researchers an opportunity to start answering the questions that matter: What happens in humans? What does the safety data show? And do the proposed benefits actually translate beyond the laboratory? Popularity isn't the same thing as proof. items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

items.title: GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?
items.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. The PROACT Phase 2 trial is studying whether an experimental drug called S-pindolol benzoate can help preserve lean body mass during semaglutide treatment. Researchers are also…

items.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
items.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. That could have implications extending well beyond weight loss. But there's an…
